name: Pelso Tamarind-Sesame Toffee Pulls
description: Hand-pulled synth-toffee ribbons with deep tamarind sourness and toasted black sesame folded through every layer. Each pull stretches to a translucent amber before snapping clean.
flavor_profile: Sour-sweet tamarind front, nutty sesame mid, caramel finish with a faint salt edge
slogan: Pull it slow. It's worth it.
cultural_context: A staple of Shelf market stalls, Pelso pulls are bought by the bag and shared communally. The act of physically stretching the candy is considered meditative by some Tier 1 regulars who eat them during long transit shifts.
story_hooks: A Pelso street vendor in the Shelf knows every regular by their preferred pull length — and has been quietly passing encoded messages in the candy wax paper for a resistance cell.
A Tier 4 food journalist goes viral after posting that Pelso pulls are better than anything sold in the Spire, causing a run on Shelf market stock and pricing out locals.
The secret to Pelso's texture is a synth-enzyme formula stolen from a corponation lab fifteen years ago — and the corporation just figured out who has it.
